changed_before_the_run: 2026-11-06, after a code review of the clean-up and before the third visit ran. A first start of the visit was stopped part way; it writes the log only at the end, so valuescale/corpus/walk.jsonl was left as it was. Changed in the code, test first: (1) the refusal of Spectronaut pivots with peptide or precursor columns is dropped. The parser read them before the clean-up, and four kept calibration pivots have such columns (PXD036468, PXD060304: EG.PrecursorId; PXD057503, PXD057796: PEP.GroupingKey); each row repeats its protein group's PG.Quantity, and the service merges the rows of one gene by their median. So expected.spectronaut's 'PXD038040 is refused in words as peptide-level' is replaced by: PXD038040 is read, kept or a later rule. The four kept pivots are outside the selection and are not visited. (2) A header is MaxQuant's with 'Majority protein IDs' and 'Gene names' spelled so, as before, or with a majority protein IDs column in any case and a MaxQuant quantity column, so a plain matrix named by 'Majority protein IDs' reads as before. All 54 MaxQuant tables in the selection have such a column. (3) MaxQuant's own spelling of a column comes first. (4) The corpus's text readers refuse what the service refuses as not text: a workbook, a binary file, UTF-16 cut mid-character. No kept table has such a head. (5) The probe chooses a header that names some quantity columns now, not one that cannot be read now. It found none of either. (6) revisit --cleanup refuses to run twice. Recomputed with this code, the selection is the same 103 records with the same reasons, so valuescale/corpus/cleanup_20261106.json stands. Every other expectation stands as written.
